newsitem.title: GERMANY: Walter-Bau says mulls another dividend cut.
newsitem.headline: Walter-Bau says mulls another dividend cut.

text.p: German construction group Walter Bau-AG on Monday confirmed a newspaper report that its founder and major shareholder, Ignaz Walter, had said the firm may reduce its dividend for 1996 for the second year in a row.
A spokesman for the company said no decision had been taken yet.
Ignaz Walter had been quoted in business daily Handelsblatt as saying the group's earnings were heavily affected by restructuring costs linked to the shedding of 1,500 jobs.
Walter was also quoted as saying group construction output rose by five percent to just under 16 billion marks in 1996.
Walter-Bau paid a dividend of seven marks per ordinary share for 1995, down from 11 marks, and cut its dividend on preference shares to eight marks from 12.

The Walter Bau group comprises construction firms Walter Bau, Dyckerhoff & Widmann AG, Heilit + Woerner Bau AG and Ed Zueblin. The stakes in those companies are held via holding company Walter Holding AG.
